Repeated architecture and checkpoint selection on the same validation users can overfit validation noise; fixing candidate sets improves pairing but does not prevent adaptive selection bias. Independent outer evaluation and privacy-based reusable holdouts address this in general, but require evaluation arrangements beyond this pinned benchmark. [Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html), [adaptive holdout research](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html). Practical recommendation here: prespecify trial limits within 43,200 GPU-seconds, configurations or proposal rules, checkpoint evaluation frequency, maximum epochs, stopping criteria, and deterministic tie-breaking. Count checkpoint comparisons as selection opportunities; these controls limit discretion without guaranteeing unbiased validation estimates.

For a paired category-stratified bootstrap, resample 200 users with replacement within each category, using identical user indices for both models; compute each category’s mean hit difference, then average the four differences equally. Pairing preserves within-user dependence ([SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). The resulting interval describes user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models and fixed candidates, assuming independent users within categories. It excludes training randomness, candidate-resampling uncertainty, and generalization to new categories. Bootstrapping the selected winner does not undo adaptive search bias or provide simultaneous coverage across tried models. With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125.

Report baseline and selected-model category scores, macro HR@10, paired differences and conditional intervals, every attempted trial including failures, checkpoint rules, seeds, selection history, and consumed compute. Label results exploratory validation evidence; test performance remains unknown until independent host evaluation. Keep the evaluator unchanged: HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures this candidate protocol, and model rankings need not match full-catalog rankings ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).
